review.summary: Phase 21 is substantive, reproducible planning/provenance work, and every one of the ten findings from the rejected phase attempt-01 is genuinely closed in current source — I verified each repair by reading bytes, not prose. The constraint-digest gate now fires on any delta whose leaf is a schema keyword regardless of kind (tools/red_team_management.py:29,162-165) with a five-case regression (tools/test_red_team_management.py:156-162); contracts/airs-retained-capabilities.json is now the current inventory plus a floorReference (red_team_management.py:354-357; artifact keys at :23501 floorReference, no seed duplication) and test_retention_output_tracks_current_additions proves --check sees additions; the dependency audit was added to the gate rather than the claim weakened (check_phase.py:166, recorded passing receipt docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json: 206 packages, advisoryRevision 999ec89d, freshHead true) and docs/CI.md:152-162,182-189 now matches the 25 executed commands with the phase-21 test exemptions removed (test_ci.py:60-67); ranged committed hygiene returned (check_phase.py:161-164) with fetch-depth 0 (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:25); the tokenizer is single-pass with nested-comment/raw-string support (red_team_management.py:211-265) and a regression using an unbalanced quote in a line comment (test:188-193); source.json is now fully verified field-by-field (verify_management_metadata:369-386) with a per-field damage test proving no field escapes; the data-plane active identity resolves through identityKind=source_metadata against a hashed source.json (:389-398, airs-active-sources.json:42-58), and that file is independently anchored because red_team_dataplane.py:65-79,608-609 cross-checks its sha256/expectedOperations against the frozen operations.json; the digest-construction procedure is documented in the module docstring, the plan (:270-278) and the rejection diagnostic itself (:165); docs/RELEASE.md:160-166 now names 0.1.1/0.2.0/0.2.1/0.2.2; private-scan history and the full eight-record review disposition are recorded in docs/phase-status.json:5148-5343. I independently confirmed the design is grounded in real bytes: all six endpoint constants match the plan table exactly (crates/scm-sdk/src/constants.rs:629-637), AudioFormat PCM16 already exists (models/red_team_data_plane.rs:989), the "already_supported" TargetMetadata audio fields genuinely exist in generated models, and the NativeConnectionParamsBase union really appends VertexAI after the five old provider branches (compatibility-decisions.json:451-474 old vs 370-396 new). All 25 recorded checks are real invocations at source ae5352b1 with exit_code 0 and match management_commands(21) element for element in order; 135 tests are green across four suites; both chunk attempt-04 records are bound to this same source hash, so chunk coverage is current and the fifth-attempt follow-up path is not needed. What holds this below the 46/50 phase floor is that both chunk attempt-04 mediums and all its lows remain open at this unchanged hash, and they sit in the central classifier: component_removed_or_renamed disposes a rename on successor existence alone, so the credential-bearing *Base request/response schemas phase 22 must implement are the only connection schemas whose new union branches carry no reviewed digest while the *RedactBase twins do; and because the digest requirement keys on path[-1], whole-subtree 'added' deltas (carrying vendor defaults multi_turn_supported:false and type const/default "client_session") plus startswith() component matching still auto-classify, which contradicts the tool's own "Fail closed on unclassified changes" docstring. Alongside that: deny.toml is the one input the newly added audit's verdict depends on that the frozen diff does not pin; the authoritative docs/PHASES.md:135 evidence cell still omits the dependency audit and ranged hygiene the gate now requires; bindings() silently overwrites duplicate keys; impl_contains accepts a private fn; two tests read stronger than they assert; and the pervasive digits-glued-to-words typography in this phase's primary deliverable documents was requested twice and is unfixed. No blocker or high finding. Categories 9/8.5/8.5/9/9 = 44/50, below the 46/50 phase floor, and 8.5/10 is below the >=9 plan gate.

findings.description: The 'removed' branch disposes a renamed component on successor *existence* alone: for len(path)==3 removals it returns component_removed_or_renamed, and build() (472-476) only asserts the successor name is present in management_spec['components']['schemas']. Nothing binds the successor's content to a reviewed digest and nothing compares the removed variant's members against it. This is not hypothetical for the current diff. I read both sides: the removed NativeConnectionParamsBase-Input (compatibility-decisions.json:413-485) declares target_connection_config.anyOf = [OpenAI, Huggingface, Databricks, BedrockAccess, MSCopilotStudio, null] and multi_turn_config.oneOf = [Stateful, Stateless]; the added successor NativeConnectionParamsBase (:328-406) declares [.., MSCopilotStudio, VertexAI, null] and [Stateful, Stateless, ClientSession]. Those are exactly the union-order and new-branch contracts the plan pins at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:94-107, yet the identical additions on the four *RedactBase schemas, which were not renamed, ARE digest-bound in REVIEWED_SEMANTIC_CHANGES (lines 39-46, 54-55). So the review gate covers the redacted response variants and leaves the credential-bearing request/response bases - the schemas phase 22 implements - unbound. The recorded decision is substantively correct (I verified the old five-provider prefix is preserved and new branches are appended ahead of the null branch only); the defect is that neither the tool nor any test enforces or records that.
findings.required_fix: For each component_removed_or_renamed delta require contains(successor, removed_value) over properties/required/type, or bind the (removed_name, successor_name) pair's successor content to a reviewed digest; additionally assert each successor union list begins with the removed variant's branch list as a prefix (ignoring the trailing null branch). Add regressions in tools/test_red_team_management.py asserting that a successor dropping a property, adding a required field, or reordering an old union prefix raises.

findings.description: The reviewed-digest requirement at 162-165 keys on path[-1] in CONSTRAINTS, so it never sees a whole-subtree delta, and the schema classifier matches by prefix. Two fail-open paths remain. (a) An added property or schema has a non-constraint leaf and reaches 192-207, returning a category with no digest review, so every default/const/additionalProperties nested inside that opaque subtree is adopted unreviewed. This already happens in the committed diff: compatibility-decisions.json:306-307 (type const+default "client_session"), :364-369 (multi_turn_supported default false, repeated on the Rest/Streaming/WebSocket bases) and the additionalProperties/default {} rows. Vendor defaults are behaviour-critical under this project's G10 policy, and the plan at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:102-104 specifically relies on the client_session default never being inserted. (b) name.startswith(...) at 194, 196 and 206 means a future component called RestConnectionParamsFoo, BasicAuthAuthConfigBar or Body_upload_baz auto-classifies without anyone reading it. Both paths contradict the function's own docstring at line 159 ("Fail closed on unclassified changes rather than silently adopting a new pin") and the drift contract the plan asserts at docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md:243-244; phase 25 inherits this classifier verbatim.
findings.required_fix: For kind=='added'/'removed' subtree deltas, require a reviewed digest over the whole identity, or recursively walk the added value and require a digest for any nested default/const/additionalProperties/enum/pattern it introduces. Replace the three startswith() prefix matches with exact name sets (the current diff has a closed, enumerable set). Add tests asserting that an unknown RestConnectionParams*-prefixed component and an added property carrying a default both raise 'Unclassified'.

findings.description: The phase-21 frozen-input list (148-153) pins crates/scm-sdk, Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, LICENSE, NOTICE and six ledgers against 0a213fe79c7f0c5758f05f53d04a5c577a4f3f4e, but not deny.toml - the license/source/ban policy consumed by the dependency audit this phase newly added at line 166. docs/checks/phase-21-dependencies.json:7 does record policySha256 b4636311..., but nothing compares that value to the audited baseline, so a relaxed policy would simply produce a new recorded hash with passed:true (206 packages) and the gate would not notice. Phase 21 changes no dependencies, so nothing is wrong in this source state; the gap is that 'unchanged SDK inputs against 0a213fe' (docs/PHASES.md:135) does not cover the configuration that decides the audit verdict.

findings.description: The phase-21 'Required evidence' cell names baseline contracts/self-tests, provenance tampering tests, generation reproducibility, the private-material scan, unchanged SDK inputs against 0a213fe and accepted chunk/phase reviews, but neither of the two obligations now in the gate: the current dependency/advisory audit (check_phase.py:166, which makes the planning gate network-dependent for RustSec refresh) and the committed-range whitespace check from the frozen baseline through HEAD (check_phase.py:161-164, which requires full Git history). docs/CI.md:145-148 documents the ranged check and :184-189 the audit, so the authoritative phase table is the least current of the three scoped documents, and this phase's own lockstep principle at docs/PHASES.md:150-151 was applied to CI.md and RELEASE.md but not to this row.

findings.description: bindings() merges three hash-pinned audit files into one dict keyed by (source, method, path) using plain assignment at 299, 309 and 311. A key present in more than one audit file is silently overwritten by the last writer, and the coverage assertion at 465 (len(rows)==160 and set(mapping) == row key set) still passes because it compares key sets, not provenance or multiplicity. The three inputs are currently disjoint by plane so no collision exists, but the collision would be invisible rather than fatal, which is inconsistent with the fail-closed posture everywhere else in this tool and with the 160-operation mapping being the phase's headline claim.
findings.required_fix: Raise on duplicate keys when merging the three audit maps (assert the key is absent before assignment) and add a test that a synthetic overlapping row fails with an explicit duplicate-binding error.

findings.description: impl_contains() matches r'\bfn\s+<method>\s*[(<]' inside a named inherent impl body and does not require pub visibility, so a private helper of the same name inside the same impl satisfies a native binding. The artifact-wide claim 'native_method_exists' written onto all 160 rows of contracts/airs-operations.json therefore proves an inherent function of that name exists, not that it is part of the public surface the mapping asserts. contracts/native-operations.json is the authoritative public ledger and is frozen by commands_for(21)[0], so this is defence-in-depth rather than an active error.
findings.required_fix: Require the matched function to be preceded by pub (with pub(crate) failing), or cross-check each (class, method) pair against contracts/native-operations.json rustMethods, and add a test that a private inherent fn of the same name does not satisfy a binding.

findings.description: The plan is this phase's primary deliverable and carries pervasive digits-glued-to-words typography: 59 occurrences of the letter-then-digit pattern in this file (line 13 '0.7.67 to0.86.0', 14 'Runtime25, Model Security41, Red Team data47 and broker5', 24 'MSRV1.89', 32 'js-yaml4.3.2', 47 ',448 native methods,23 default bindings,14', 252 'total>=42/50 (aim45)'), plus a comma splice at lines 50-51 ('...airs-0.2.2-retention.json`, The output is the current inventory'). The same pattern occurs 34 times in docs/PHASES.md and in docs/implementation-plan.md:177-179 ('phases21-25', 'completed0.2.2 delivery', 'management0.86.0 target contracts', 'version0.2.3'). This was raised in the governance chunk attempt-04 (required fix: 'in the same qualified source change') and in the provenance chunk attempt-04 and is unfixed at this hash. It also makes the regex count guards at tools/test_ci.py:118-128,135-146 fragile, because the same glueing inside one of those asserted sentences would turn a lockstep guard into an unexplained failure.
findings.required_fix: Proofread docs/red-team-management-0.86-plan.md, docs/PHASES.md, docs/CI.md, docs/RELEASE.md and docs/implementation-plan.md for missing spaces before numerals and the comma splice at plan lines 50-51, keeping the guarded count sentences in their asserted form.

findings.description: In test_future_milestones_require_explicit_complete_artifacts, self.assertFalse(any("0.2.2" in c for c in commands)) tests list membership, not substring containment: c is a command list, so it only fails when some argument is exactly "0.2.2". A rewritten but still version-bound argument such as docs/checks/phase-23-release-registry-0.2.2.json would pass. The same shape at line 154 ('scripts/check-rust.py' in c) is correct only incidentally, because that value is a standalone element. Nothing leaks today - the only 0.2.2 literal arrives with scripts/check-access-release.py, which management_commands skips at check_phase.py:186 - so this is assertion precision, but the test reads as a guarantee it does not provide for the inherited phase-22-25 lists.
findings.required_fix: Replace the membership checks with argument-level substring checks, e.g. any("0.2.2" in value for c in commands for value in c), and apply the same form to the historical-receipt-path assertions at lines 157-160.

findings.description: test_node_matches_owned_pin_and_phase_gate_verifies_only asserts only that 'tools/bootstrap_reference.py' appears somewhere in the workflow text. Because CI is routed at commands_for(21), two of the 25 executed commands are '.local/typescript/node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/schema-oracle.mts --check' and 'tools/node_modules/.bin/tsx tools/verify-gateway-specimens.mts --check', neither of which exists until bootstrap_reference.py restores the frozen tree. The ordering is correct today (.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:70-73 places the restore immediately before the gate at :73) but it is unguarded, while the analogous cargo prerequisite ordering is asserted by index at test_ci.py:166-169. Moving the restore after the gate would break the contracts job with every test still green.
findings.required_fix: Resolve the contracts job step list and assert lines.index('run: python3 tools/bootstrap_reference.py') < lines.index(phase) whenever any selected command's argv[0] resolves under .local/typescript/node_modules or tools/node_modules, mirroring test_qualification_prepares_complete_locked_graph_before_offline_checks.

findings.description: private_scan_history now records the authoritative receipt and seven superseded ones, which closes the structural part of phase attempt-01 finding 10, but all seven entries carry the identical reason string 'Retained prior source scan; superseded by review repairs. Interrupted scan has no acceptance claim.' That text is applied unchanged to -initial, -pre-oracle and -pre-scope-correction, which were not interrupted, and the one entry with passed:false (-interrupted, 5325-5329) is indistinguishable in rationale from the six passing ones. The required fix asked for 'the reason each was regenerated'; a single boilerplate sentence repeated seven times does not let a reader tell why each receipt was superseded, which is the information the names themselves ('pre-oracle', 'pre-scope-correction') hint at.
findings.required_fix: Give each history entry its own specific reason naming what changed between it and its successor (oracle corpus rebinding, chunk scope correction, interruption), or reduce the set to the gate-verified receipt plus one provenance note that enumerates the regeneration causes in order.

findings.description: The condition 'if phase == 21 or any(command[:3] == ["git", "diff", "--check"] and any(".." in word for word in command[3:]) for command in commands_for(phase))' now contains a dead disjunct: commands_for(21) includes the ranged check at check_phase.py:161-164, so the generic any(...) clause is already true for phase 21 and the hardcoded branch guards nothing. It was presumably needed while phase 21 had no ranged command. Leaving a version-specific special case in a lockstep guard invites the opposite failure later: if a future phase drops its ranged check, the hardcoded 21 keeps asserting fetch-depth 0 for a requirement that no longer exists.
findings.required_fix: Delete the 'phase == 21 or' disjunct so the fetch-depth requirement is derived purely from whether a selected command contains a commit range, and keep test_current_dependency_audit_and_committed_hygiene_are_required as the assertion that phase 21 actually has one.

limitations: Read-only Read/Glob/Grep with no shell: I could not recompute the reviewed source fingerprint ae5352b1..., the checks snapshot hash 36ce2f96..., or any file sha256, and I could not re-execute any of the 25 checks or the four test suites. I verified evidence by reading the recorded invocations, exit codes and captured output, by reconstructing management_commands(21) by hand and comparing it element for element and in order against the recorded list, and by independently cross-reading the artifacts those commands assert over.

Static evidence only, as the artifacts themselves state. Native-binding verification proves a named inherent method exists; it does not prove request construction, generated Rust correctness, wire acceptance or tenant permissions. The five response-declaration fixtures, both response modes, typed round-trips, old-consumer source compatibility, MSRV/current-compiler regressions and live acceptance belong to phases 22-24 and were not judged. I did not treat later-phase operations marked planned as missing phase-21 deliverables.

No remote CI run of the re-pointed phase-21 workflow exists. Phase-21 CI coverage is committed configuration plus local guard evidence; docs/CI.md:216-219 and docs/PHASES.md:174-180 state this honestly and I did not treat a terminal remote run as a phase-21 requirement. I likewise did not re-audit historical release infrastructure: the only historical item I assessed is docs/RELEASE.md:160-166, because phase 20's accepted outcome required it to be scheduled in the next qualified source change and it is declared phase-21 chunk scope.
